clue.text: A crawler will go around most of the deck

indicators.note: the word go is split open to hold the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only part of the word deck is wanted, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Some creeping creature is going to wander round most of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' takes the D from DECK, leaving ECK, and 'around' puts GO round it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small lizard climbs walls and ceilings, so it is a creeping animal.

clue.text: I barge about before everyone comes back to see her

indicators.note: about signals the letters of I barge are moved around into a new order
comes back tells us the word for everyone is read from the end to the start

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone shoves their way past before the whole crowd returns to visit a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I BARGE into GABRIE; 'comes back' turns ALL into LLA, which follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, so the pronoun for a woman stands in for it.

clue.text: Old vehicle travelling daily with article in ramshackle cab

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning lady, also called a char

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the shuffled letters of cab
ramshackle means tumbledown, so the letters of cab are knocked into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old coach carrying a cleaner, with a grammatical article inside a battered taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' rearranges CAB to ABC, and 'in' sets AN inside it after the B, giving ABANC after CHAR. 'travelling' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for outings and excursions.

clue.text: River in northern France runs alternatively to two points

parts.note: alternatively means or
N and E are two compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A French river flows either one way or towards two compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: This river flows through Normandy into the English Channel near Caen.

clue.text: No fish around along the sea shore

indicators.note: around shows the fishing phrase wraps round the letter for nothing

parts.note: to fish is to cast a line
O is a nought, zero, nothing

explanation.surface: There are no fish to be found anywhere along the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is a verb giving CAST LINE, and 'around' wraps it round O for 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge where land meets the sea is the shore, a synonym.

clue.text: Risk being badly beaten at tennis

definitions.meaning: to risk ruin is to invite catastrophe
a heavy defeat on a tennis surface is a calamity on the playing area

explanation.definitionFit: To court something is to invite it, so inviting calamity is risking; literally, a tennis rout is a calamity on court.

clue.text: This is not now the point

parts.note: taken as written
N is a compass point, north

explanation.surface: A philosopher remarks that this is not the present moment, which is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: At another time, past or future, rather than the present.

clue.text: Main meal wasn't started by those inside

indicators.note: wasn't started shows the opening letter of the meal is dropped

parts.note: the main meal of the day is dinner

explanation.surface: The evening meal never got going for the people indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner means interior, situated within, as the inner rooms of a house.

clue.text: Gas which makes the cook hesitate

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters of the are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: A fume that makes the chef pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is the anagram signal, turning THE into ETH before ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile anaesthetic vapour, once widely used in surgery.

clue.text: Draw away after nerve centre moved abroad for better conditions

indicators.note: after places the word for drawing away behind the nerve centre

parts.note: the brain is the body's nerve centre
to drain is to draw off liquid

explanation.surface: Something pulls away after the control room has been moved overseas for better facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the phenomenon of skilled people emigrating rather than giving a noun outright.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the emigration of skilled or educated people seeking better pay and conditions overseas.

clue.text: Then met up somehow this time, after countless previous such occasions

definitions.text: this time, after countless previous such occasions

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of then met up are rearranged by some means

explanation.surface: We then met up again, for what felt like the hundredth time.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming after an indefinitely large number in a series; the latest of very many.

clue.text: Make pointer meet to measure the power with it

indicators.note: make tells us to form something new from the letters of pointer meet to

explanation.surface: Get a gauge's needle to meet its mark when measuring the power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal for POINTER MEET TO.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures electrical potential, the force driving current in a circuit.

clue.text: I take commercial vehicle-a terrible one!

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle for goods

explanation.surface: I get a delivery van, and a dreadful one at that!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Ivan the Terrible, Tsar of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian tsar remembered by history with the epithet 'the Terrible' bore this name.

clue.text: Express the condition

definitions.meaning: to express is to say or declare
a condition is a situation or circumstance

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to put into words; as a noun, the condition or situation something is in.

clue.text: Brother in sombre raiment, as you'd expect

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words sombre raiment

explanation.surface: A monk dressed in dark clothes, just as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you'd expect' reflects the apt picture of a friar in dark robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Southern US dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit of the Uncle Remus tales.

clue.text: Range of opportunity

definitions.meaning: opportunity means room or freedom to act

explanation.definitionFit: It means both the extent of something and the freedom or room for action.

clue.text: See 8 across
Game to sell the spanner

parts.note: to auction is to sell to the highest bidder
a bridge spans a river or gap

explanation.surface: A match in which a wrench is put up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like a tool but means something that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: An older form of the card game in which players bid for the contract.

clue.text: Not the place to take evening classes

definitions.text: Not the place to take evening classes

parts.words: Not the place to take evening classes
parts.note: an establishment that teaches only in daylight hours would be the wrong venue for night study

explanation.definitionFit: Such a school educates pupils who go home at night, unlike boarders; it holds lessons in daytime.

clue.text: It is necessary to line seats up properly

indicators.note: set up properly signals the letters of line seats are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Seats must be arranged in neat rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable or required; a necessity.

clue.text: Admit skill at meeting the bill

parts.note: to admit is to accept
skill means ability

explanation.surface: Owning up to talent while paying the invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting the bill' is the idiom for being suitable, not paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfactory or adequate, as something that fits the bill is.

clue.text: Gather food for schoolchildren

definitions.meaning: British school slang for snacks and sweets

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools this word means sweets and snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a fold stitched into cloth, and British school slang for snacks.

clue.text: Records a monkey in a back street

indicators.note: in places the monkey inside the turned street abbreviation
back shows the abbreviation for street is read in the other direction

parts.note: an ape is a type of primate, loosely a monkey

explanation.surface: Discs feature a primate in an alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS and 'in' puts APE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Recordings made on magnetic cassettes or reels.

clue.text: Repeatedly turn large milk container

definitions.meaning: to stir or agitate over and over
a big metal can for transporting milk

explanation.definitionFit: It means to agitate milk or cream repeatedly, and the big can farmers once carried milk in.

clue.text: Mark of character

explanation.definitionFit: It means a printed impression and also the distinctive nature, as 'a man of his kind'.

clue.text: I study an image

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning

explanation.surface: I examine a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious painting or symbol; a likeness or representation.

clue.text: Only a very small Greek character

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: It is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet and, by extension, a tiny amount.

clue.text: The opposite of two of each

definitions.text: The opposite of two of each

parts.words: The opposite of two of each
parts.note: a word meaning the pair together, contrasted with taking them singly one by one

explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to two things together, whereas each refers to them individually.

clue.text: Idiot about to cast clout is one with lots of money

indicators.note: about shows the word for idiot surrounds the rest

parts.note: prat is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: to cast is to throw into new shape, so the letters of clout are reworked

explanation.surface: A fool is about to throw a punch at a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cast' rearranges CLOUT into LUTOC, and 'about' places it inside PRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power derives from wealth.

clue.text: French fly in about ten carrying rounded mouldings

indicators.note: carrying shows the reversed figures hold the French word
about tells us the digits for ten are read backwards

parts.note: ten written as figures is 1 and 0, read as I and O
vol is French for flight, from voler, to fly

explanation.surface: A French insect in roughly ten bearing curved architectural trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IO (ten as 1, 0) into OI, which is 'carrying' VOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Convex architectural mouldings of quarter-circle profile, the plural of ovolo.

clue.text: One who finds that heat burns

definitions.text: One who finds that heat burns

parts.words: One who finds that heat burns
parts.note: a person lying out in hot weather discovers the effect of the sun on skin; the words heat burns also rearrange to give the solution

explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in sunshine to tan may well discover that strong sunlight scorches skin.

clue.text: One way to kill animals putting a hall in uproar!

indicators.note: in uproar suggests chaos, so the letters of a hall are thrown about

explanation.surface: A slaughter method that causes a riot in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat prepared according to Islamic law, slaughtered in the prescribed manner.
